name: java-service
description: A Java web service, most commonly Spring Boot, built with Maven or Gradle and packaged as an executable jar or war.

runtimes.version: <the JDK version declared in the build file>
runtimes.provision: <the matching JDK installed on dev and prod hosts>

services.manager: <a service manager or a container runtime>
services.bind: <loopback-only, unless a trusted edge forwards identity>

routing.staticRoot: <built frontend output folder, if the service also serves static assets>

files: <a per-environment application config file, kept out of version control for real environments>
config.rule: real settings files are gitignored; a committed example config file shows the shape only

data.migrations: <the app's migration tool, e.g. Flyway or Liquibase, or none>
data.state: <an external database; nothing durable lives on the app host itself>

deploy.script: <deploy script: build, stop, swap the jar, start>
verify: the health endpoint returns a body with a status field, not just HTTP 200
a rendered page or response payload changed, so an old artefact behind a restarted process cannot pass
